flashcards.a: Per-second billing with a 1-minute minimum. Resource-based pricing since 2018: machine types bill as separate vCPU and memory SKUs, enabling custom machine types at ~5% premium.

flashcards.q: Sustained Use Discount tiers and max?
flashcards.a: Automatic per-region credits aggregated across eligible VMs: 0-25% of month full price, then incremental discounts on 25-50/50-75/75-100 tiers, netting up to ~30% for full-month usage. Excludes E2, GPUs, App Engine/Dataflow VMs, CUD-covered usage.

flashcards.q: Spot VMs: discount and eviction contract?
flashcards.a: 60-91% below on-demand; Compute Engine may reclaim capacity at any time with a 30-second ACPI termination notice. Spot prices adjust at most once per month. Successor to preemptible VMs.

Resource-based (commit vCPU/memory in region): 1yr ~28%, 3yr ~57%+ depending on family. Spend-based flexible CUDs commit $/hour across services including Cloud Run/GKE. CUDs bill regardless of actual usage.
$0.10/hr (~$73/month) per cluster in Standard AND Autopilot; the first zonal Standard cluster per billing account is free.
Roughly $0.0445/vCPU-hr + $0.0049/GiB-hr with 1-second granularity, management premium of ~10-20% baked in. Idle pods cost nothing; requests ARE the bill.

flashcards.q: What flips Autopilot pods to per-node billing?
flashcards.a: Pods requesting special hardware - GPUs, TPUs, or named machine series - bill per whole node plus premium, like Standard. The pay-per-request advantage vanishes exactly where costs are highest.

Hard: no privileged containers/elevated access, no node SSH, COS-only, regional-only clusters, no Windows. Outdated claims: GPUs/TPUs (ComputeClass), Spot pods, Arm T2A, non-elevated DaemonSets, Confidential Nodes, default gVisor all work now.

flashcards.q: Where is the Standard-vs-Autopilot cost crossover?
flashcards.a: Somewhere around moderate-to-high sustained utilization - analyses place it anywhere from ~50% to ~80% depending on packing assumptions. Nobody credible gives one number; measure your p50 node utilization first.

flashcards.q: What does Batch add over raw VMs for jobs?
flashcards.a: Queueing, array-job/task semantics, dependency graphs, automatic provisioning incl. Spot and GPU shapes, teardown after completion. Not for streaming or low-latency serving - GKE/Dataflow territory.

flashcards.q: What happens during a 3x traffic spike on Standard?
flashcards.a: HPA scales pods in seconds against existing headroom; pending pods trigger node provisioning at 1-3 min lag (~), longer for GPU. The spike gap is served by buffer capacity - the strandedness that makes Standard expensive.

Google's custom offload processors handling storage/networking/security workloads offloaded from CPUs, introduced with N4/C4 generation (2024). Newer families show better price-performance at high IOPS.
